job_description_info.job_description:
# Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform

**Company:** Tessel Cargo Software (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Antwerp, Belgium (hybrid, 2 days/week in office) – candidates based elsewhere in the EU may work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent
**Team:** Routing & Tracking (7 engineers, 1 engineering manager, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Tessel Cargo Software builds the software that mid-sized freight forwarders use to plan, route and track shipments across Europe. Our Routing & Tracking team owns the services that turn thousands of carrier events per minute into a reliable live picture of where every container, trailer and parcel is.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a few years of solid production experience to help us grow this platform. You will work on event ingestion, route-optimisation APIs and the customer-facing tracking API, and you will be on the on-call rota (one week in six, supported by a runbook-driven team).

## What you will do

- Design, build and maintain Python (FastAPI) services that ingest carrier events from EDI, REST webhooks and message queues
- Own parts of our PostgreSQL data model and write migrations that are safe to run on live data
- Improve the performance and reliability of our public tracking API (currently ~400 requests/second at peak)
- Work with the data team to expose clean event streams (Kafka) for analytics and ETA prediction
- Write automated tests, review code and contribute to our CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
- Help investigate production incidents and write blameless post-mortems
- Take part in architecture discussions and document decisions in short design notes

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python (or a comparable language such as Go, Java or Kotlin, if you are happy to work mainly in Python)
- Solid experience with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including query tuning and schema migrations
- Experience designing and consuming REST APIs
- Experience with Docker and deploying services to a cloud environment (we use AWS)
- Practical understanding of automated testing and CI/CD
- Good written and spoken English; you can explain technical trade-offs clearly

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- Experience with Kubernetes (we run on EKS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)
- Exposure to observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
- Knowledge of logistics, transport or supply-chain domains, or EDI formats (EDIFACT, X12)
- Dutch or French language skills

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 62,000 – 82,000 gross per year depending on experience
- 28 days of holiday, a learning budget of EUR 1,500 per year and a home-office allowance
- Pension scheme, public-transport card and a modern hybrid office near Antwerpen-Centraal
- A team that values pragmatic engineering, clear documentation and sustainable pace

## How to apply

Send us your CV and, if you like, a short cover letter or links to code you are proud of. We read every application and reply within two weeks. Our interviews are: a 30-minute intro call, a practical technical conversation about a past project and a short system-design discussion.

Tessel Cargo Software is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.

company_info.company_description:
Tessel Cargo Software is an Antwerp-based logistics technology company founded in 2017. It builds software for freight forwarders to plan routes and loads, book carriers, track shipments in real time, and digitise delivery notes and customs paperwork. Its products help reduce manual work and give forwarders’ customers clearer shipment updates. More than 340 forwarders across 19 countries use its tools.

The company operates in freight technology and supply-chain software. It has 120 employees across Antwerp and Poznań, alongside a remote-first engineering group, and is expanding its tracking platform and engineering team. Its systems process large volumes of shipment events, making reliability, scalability and service ownership important.

Tessel’s stated values are **“Be dependable. Say what you see. Leave it better.”** Its engineering culture emphasizes small product teams, practical communication, and taking responsibility for the software teams build and run. Engineers contribute to service reliability and on-call operations; the company also shares engineering knowledge through its blog and supports a local Python meetup.

## Tessel Cargo Software raises EUR 24 million to expand live tracking across Europe
**Antwerp, 12 March 2026**

Tessel Cargo Software, the Antwerp-based provider of routing and tracking software for freight forwarders, announced a EUR 24 million Series B round. The funding will be used to double the engineering team by the end of 2027, extend the Tessel Track API with predictive ETAs and open a second engineering hub in Poznań.

"Forwarders still lose hours every day to chasing status updates," said co-founder and CEO Margot Vandenberg. "Our goal is that a dispatcher never has to phone a driver to ask where a trailer is."

CTO Piotr Lis said the company is migrating its event pipeline from queue-based workers to Kafka streams to support peak loads during the autumn peak season, and is investing in observability and on-call tooling. "We want engineers who enjoy running the things they build," he added.

Tessel says it processed 38 million shipment events per day in February 2026, up 2.4x from a year earlier, and that its tracking API maintained 99.95% availability over the last twelve months.
# Careers at Tessel Cargo Software
*(fictional careers page – tesselcargo.example/careers)*

## Build the software behind Europe's supply chains

**Engineering at Tessel**
- Stack: Python (FastAPI), Go for a few high-throughput workers, PostgreSQL, Kafka, AWS (EKS, RDS, S3), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Grafana/Prometheus/OpenTelemetry
- Team structure: product teams of 6-8 engineers with an engineering manager and a product manager

Rafael Moretti-Klein
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) position on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing & Tracking team. The role’s focus on reliable event ingestion and tracking-related backend systems closely matches my experience building high-volume backend systems in Python and Go, including services that process data from 300,000 vehicles.

At Nordfels Telematik, I built fleet-telematics backend systems using Python, C++, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ, ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles. At Streamhaus, I served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python and designed a Go entitlement service that handled 120,000 requests per second at peak. As Director of Engineering, I drove the migration from a Python 2 monolith to around 60 Python and Go services on GKE, improving playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. These experiences have given me a strong foundation in event-driven systems, API reliability and the practical trade-offs involved in scaling services.

I would bring hands-on Python expertise, experience with PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry, as well as a record of improving service ownership and engineering practices. At Streamhaus, I introduced architecture reviews and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide; earlier, I built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years. Tessel’s emphasis on dependable services, clear documentation and service ownership matches my experience introducing RFCs, architecture reviews, Python service standards and on-call guidelines.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend and platform experience could contribute to Tessel’s shipment-tracking platform. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It opens with a clear connection to shipment tracking, uses strong quantified evidence (300,000 vehicles, 120,000 requests per second, approximately 60 services, and 99.5% to 99.95% availability), and maintains a credible technical focus. The examples are relevant to event ingestion, API reliability, Python services, and operational engineering. The main content limitation is that some required capabilities are only implied or omitted, particularly automated testing, PostgreSQL depth, and the specific evidence behind the phrase “service ownership.”
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly in structure: standard headings are unnecessary for a short letter, the text is plain, readable, and contains many relevant keywords including Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, GKE, API, event-driven systems, and on-call. AI screening probability is high for the role's domain and seniority signals. Screening may be reduced by the absence of explicit supported wording such as “automated testing,” “PostgreSQL/PostGIS,” “FastAPI,” and “relational databases.” Do not add Docker, CI/CD, REST, query tuning, or schema migrations unless the candidate can substantiate them.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for Python backend engineering, high-volume event ingestion, logistics and telematics, API reliability, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, on-call practices, architecture documentation, and clear technical standards. The Nordfels experience is especially relevant to shipment tracking because it involved fleet telematics and GPS data from 300,000 vehicles. The letter also reflects several cultural themes from the advertisement, including dependable services, documentation, architecture decisions, and service operations. Candidate-material gaps remain for PostgreSQL query tuning and schema migrations, Docker, AWS deployment specifically, CI/CD, and Dutch or French. REST API design and consumption are not explicitly evidenced in the supplied candidate material. These are job-alignment gaps rather than defects to be solved through unsupported wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR CONTENT/ATS IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the third paragraph, change “I would bring hands-on Python expertise, experience with PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry” to “I would bring hands-on Python expertise, including FastAPI, experience with PostgreSQL/PostGIS and Kafka, and experience with Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry.” This uses supported terms from the candidate information and improves keyword precision.
2. In the third paragraph, replace “a record of improving service ownership and engineering practices” with “a record of improving service reliability and engineering practices.” The revised wording is directly supported by the documented availability improvement, on-call guidelines, RFC process, and architecture review board; “improving service ownership” is not explicitly demonstrated.
3. In the third paragraph, revise “earlier, I built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years” to “earlier, I built an automated Python test harness used by QA for eight years.” This makes the candidate’s documented automated-testing experience explicit without claiming CI/CD experience.
4. In the second paragraph, change “These experiences have given me a strong foundation in event-driven systems, API reliability and the practical trade-offs involved in scaling services” to “These experiences have given me a strong foundation in event ingestion, message-queue-based systems, API reliability and the practical trade-offs involved in scaling services.” This more closely mirrors the advertisement while remaining supported by GPS ingestion and RabbitMQ experience.
